CSA: Control sector area; an airspace sector defined for ATC operational purposes.
CSM: Control and status monitoring; continuous monitoring of aircraft systems or ATC equipment status.
CSP: Control sector position; a specific ATC workstation or sector within a control area.
CSW: Control stopway; a paved area beyond the runway end designed to stop aircraft in an aborted takeoff.
CT: Control; the authority to direct aircraft movement or the act of exercising such authority.
CTA: Control area; a controlled airspace extending upward from a specified lower limit.
CTAF: Common traffic advisory frequency; a frequency used at non-towered airports for aircraft-to-aircraft communications.
CTL: Control; abbreviation used in flight plans and ATC communications to denote control authority.
CTM: Control and monitoring; combined function of controlling and monitoring aircraft or systems.
CTP: Control point; a designated point used for ATC coordination and boundary definition.
CTRY: Country; used in flight plans to indicate the nationality or registration country of an aircraft.
CTZ: Control zone; a controlled airspace extending upward from the surface around an aerodrome.
CU: Cumulus; a type of cloud characterized by vertical development, often associated with convective activity.
CUF: Cumuliform; cloud formations with vertical development characteristic of cumulus-type clouds.
CUST: Customs; government inspection authority at international airports handling arriving passengers and cargo.
CV: Control vector; an ATC-issued heading and/or altitude assignment to guide aircraft along a desired path.
CW: Continuous wave; a radio transmission mode used for Morse code and NDB navigation signals.
CWC: Ceiling and visibility okay (CAVOK); a meteorological condition where visibility is 10 km or more, no cloud below 5000 ft, and no significant weather.
CWO: Carriage of weapons; authorization or restriction concerning weapons carried on board an aircraft.
D: Down; used in aviation to indicate a downward direction, e.g., wind shear down or gear down.
D-W: Demand and wait; a communication protocol where a transmission is made on demand followed by a waiting period.
D/ATT: Direct-attach; a type of connection or interface where a device is directly attached without intermediary systems.
DAL: Declared; used in the context of declared distances (TORA, TODA, ASDA, LDA) published for each runway.
DB: Decibel; a logarithmic unit used to measure sound intensity or signal power ratio in communications.
DBRK: Debarkation; the process of leaving an aircraft after landing, also known as disembarkation.
DCLT: Declutter; the removal of non-essential information from a radar display to improve situational awareness.
DCT: Direct; clearance to proceed directly to a waypoint or fix without following published routing.
DD: Dangerous goods; hazardous materials that require special handling and documentation for air transport.
DDH: Decision distance (Decision Height); the height above runway threshold at which a missed approach must be initiated if visual reference is not established.
DE: Germany; ICAO country code prefix used in aircraft registration and flight plan nationality fields.
DEC: Declination; the angular difference between true north and magnetic north at a given location.
DECEL: Deceleration; the rate at which an aircraft reduces speed, relevant to landing and approach planning.
DEI: Diversity; a technique using multiple antennas or frequencies to improve signal reception reliability.
DEL: Delivery; the ATC clearance delivery position responsible for issuing IFR clearances to departing aircraft.
DEP: Departure; the phase of flight from takeoff to the initial climb segment, or the ATC departure control function.
DEPT: Department; used in aviation documentation and flight plans to denote an organizational department.
DER: Departure end of runway; the runway threshold opposite the landing threshold, used for obstacle clearance calculations.
DES: Descend; ATC instruction or pilot action to reduce altitude, typically at a specified rate.
DESC: Describe; used in aviation reports to provide additional detail about weather phenomena or system status.
DEST: Destination; the final airport or waypoint where a flight is scheduled to arrive.
DET: Detach; to separate or disconnect a component, or to release from a formation or assignment.
DEV: Deviation; the difference between planned and actual track, heading, or altitude, or magnetic compass error.
DF: Direction finding; a radio navigation technique that determines the bearing of a radio signal source.
DH: Decision height; the minimum height on an instrument approach at which a missed approach must be executed if visual references are not acquired.
DHSV: Decision height; same as DH, used in some automated systems and documentation (duplicate abbreviation).
DIF: Diffuse; describing precipitation or clouds that are widespread and not clearly defined in boundaries.
DIS: Distance; the spatial separation between two points, used in navigation and separation standards.
DISCH: Discharge; the release of electrical charge from an aircraft or the unloading of cargo/passengers.
DISP: Displace; to shift position, as in a displaced threshold or displaced landing zone.
DIST: Distance; the measured or calculated length between two geographic points or positions.
